title: Karyotype
what: This is a blood test from a vein. The lab counts and looks at your chromosomes, which carry your genetic information.
why: For infertility, repeated miscarriages, before IVF, or if a child may have a genetic condition.
duration: the blood draw takes 3 to 5 minutes; results usually come in 2 to 4 weeks
tell_doctor: If you are ill or have a fever now
If you take antibiotics or hormones
If genetic conditions run in your family

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: It is best to test when you are well. If you were recently ill, ask your doctor when to come.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no need to fast, but avoid fatty food before the test. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

bring: Past genetic test results, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow, and the skin is wiped
Blood is drawn into a special tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Results usually come in 2 to 4 weeks, because the cells need to be grown
It is best to discuss the result with a geneticist

faq.q: Why does the test take so long?
faq.a: Blood cells are grown for several days. Then their chromosomes are studied under a microscope.

faq.q: If my karyotype is normal, does that mean no genetic problems?
faq.a: Not always. A karyotype shows large changes. Smaller ones are found with other tests, if needed.

reminders.text: Karyotype test tomorrow. If you are ill now, call the clinic.
